text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Naturalist JOHANN FORSTER, who accompanied Captain JAMES COOK on his second voyage in the "Resolution", was born in 1729.
Hungarian pianist and composer FRANZ LISZT was born in 1811. He spent the last 20 years of his life as a Franciscan monk.
French stage actress SARAH BERNHARDT was born in 1844. She was very popular and continued her successful career even after the loss of a leg.

South Australian radical politician CHARLES KINGSTON was born in 1850. He challenged a conservative opponent to a pistol duel, but the opponent called the police and KINGSTON was arrested in Victoria Square in Adelaide.
British actress JOAN FONTAINE, who was initially typecast as a shy English rose, was born in 1917. She won an Oscar nomination for "Rebecca" and an Oscar for her role in "The Constant Nymph".
Novelist DORIS LESSING was born in Persia to British parents in 1919.

United States singer and actress ANNETTE FUNICELLO was born in 1942. She became a member of the Walt Disney Organisation, the Mouseketeers, and made her televsion debut in a pair of Mickey Mouse Ears. Her first hit was produced by the Disney label in 1959. It was "Tall Paul". Other hits included "O Dio Mio" (1960) and "Pineapple Princess" (1960). She appeared beside FRANKIE AVALON in a number of Beach Movies and in 1976 had a regular television show "Easy Does It". In 1987 she returned in the film "Back to the Beach" again with FRANKIE AVALON.
French actress CATHERINE DENEUVE was born in 1943. Her films include "Belle de Jour".
** EVENTS **
1797 : ANDRE JACQUES GARNERIN made the first successful

parachute descent from a balloon in Paris. During his descent GARNERIN swung back and forth like a pendulum and was violently ill on several spectators gathered beneath to watch the spectacle. 1872 : The Overland Telegraph line was opened. It was a

very important day in Australia's history as it meant that messages couldn be sent and received from the rest of the world at high speed. Before 1872 the only link Australia had with the rest of the world was the monthly sea mail service.
1909 : ELISE DEROCHE became the first woman to fly solo.
1910 : DR HAWLEY HAWLEY CRIPPEN was found guilty of
murdering his wife.
1917 : The Trans-Australian Railway was opened, running
from Kalgoorlie to Port Augusta.
1934 : American gangster "Pretty Boy" Floyd was killed by
FBI agents.
1937 : The Duke of Windsor and his wife WALLIS made a

controversial visit to ADOLF HITLER at Berchtesgaden in Bavaria. The unofficial tour caused much comment in British government circles. The Royal couple were reportedly impressed with the Nazi achievements such as workers' housing and full employment.
1958 : The 500,000th Holden to be built was handed over
to the Royal Flying Doctor Service.
1962 : ANC leader NELSON MANDELA went on trial in South

Africa for treason. He pleaded not guilty, but was convicted and jailed in 1964. He was released in February 1990 and the ban on the ANC was lifted. He was elected the first black leader of the country after the first free elections in 1994.
1966 : KGB master spy GEORGE BLAKE escaped for a maximum

security prison in London. The former M16 officer had spied for the Soviets for 12 years. In 1962 he was sentenced to 42 years imprisonment - representing one year for each of the lives his actions were estimated to have cost.
1979 : The British government announced it would outlaw
"insider trading" on the stockmarket.
1981 : Australia told the United States it would join the
Sinai peace-keeping force if Canada and Britain took part.
1987 : The World-wide stock market crash continued with
share prices plummetting in London.
